issues.legal_issue: Land already vested in the government through a completed acquisition is not divested, and the acquisition does not lapse because a later general acquisition law applies or an award is delayed.
material_facts: A final acquisition notification was published under the state urban-improvement law, and the land vested in the government before the general land-acquisition law was extended to the state.
The awards were made after that extension, and the owners contended that they were outside the applicable time limit.
The later state amendments provided transitional rules for pending acquisitions, including rules on awards and compensation.
issues.conclusion: The later extension and amendments did not divest land that had already vested. The acquisition did not lapse even if the award was not made within the later statutory period; non-compliance with the transitional requirements also did not undo the vesting.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 52(4) of the Rajasthan Urban Improvement Act, publication of the final notification vested the land absolutely in the State, free from encumbrances. The subsequent extension of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and the transitional provisions in Section 60-A of the state Act could not divest that completed vesting. Section 11-A of the Land Acquisition Act did not cause the acquisition to lapse after vesting. The Court relied on the analogous vesting principles in Section 17 and on Satendra Prasad Jain v. State of U.P. (1993) 4 SCC 369, P. Chinnanna v. State of A.P. (1994) 5 SCC 486, and Awadh Bihari Yadav v. State of Bihar (1995) 6 SCC 31.

rule.if: land_acquisition_proceeding and final_notice_published_and_vesting_occurred and vesting_preceded_later_law and award_was_delayed

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns a government proceeding to acquire land.
predicates.final_notice_published_and_vesting_occur: The acquiring government published a final acquisition notice that caused the land to vest in it.
predicates.vesting_preceded_later_law: The land vested before a later change made a general acquisition regime applicable to the area.
predicates.award_was_delayed: The award was made after the period later said to govern its making had passed.

issues.definition: When a land-acquisition proceeding has resulted in vesting before a later legal change and the award is delayed, the acquisition remains effective.

issues.legal_issue: Land may be acquired for a public purpose under the urban-improvement law without a formulated improvement scheme.
material_facts: The land was acquired for multipurpose development, including residential, commercial, and industrial construction.
The owners challenged the acquisition on the grounds that no scheme had been framed and that the acquisition was inconsistent with the planned use of the land.
The acquisition notification identified development purposes under the urban-improvement law.
issues.conclusion: The absence of a formulated or finalized scheme did not invalidate the acquisition for a public purpose under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 52(1) of the Rajasthan Urban Improvement Act authorizes acquisition when the State Government considers land necessary for improvement or another purpose under the Act. Relying on Gandhi Grah Nirman Sahkari Samiti Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan (1993) 2 SCC 662, the Court held that framing a scheme is mandatory when the Trust undertakes the work, but the State Government may undertake development without a scheme under Chapter V. The Court considered State of Tamil Nadu v. A. Mohammed Yousef (1991) 4 SCC 224 distinguishable in light of the decision concerning the Rajasthan Act.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns a government proceeding to acquire land.
predicates.government_acquired_for_public_purpose: The government acquired land for a development purpose it identified as public.
predicates.no_scheme_was_formulated: No improvement scheme had been prepared or finalized for the proposed work.

issues.definition: If the government acquires land for a public development purpose without a formulated scheme, the acquisition can remain valid without that scheme.

issues.legal_issue: A prior lower-court view that has been disapproved by a later larger bench and remains under review does not establish that an acquisition is invalid.
material_facts: The owners relied on an earlier division-bench decision that had quashed acquisition notifications on the basis that acquisition required a sanctioned scheme.
Special leave petitions against that decision were pending before the Supreme Court.
A later full bench of the same High Court disagreed with the earlier decision’s reading of Supreme Court authority.
issues.conclusion: The earlier division-bench decision did not affect the acquisitions and did not state the correct law; the later full-bench view was correct.
issues.legal_principle: The Court noted that the earlier decision was under challenge and had not been approved by the later full bench. On the merits, it held that the earlier decision misread Gandhi Grah Nirman Sahkari Samiti Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan (1993) 2 SCC 662, whose combined reasoning supported acquisition without a scheme where the State Government acted for a purpose authorized by the Rajasthan Urban Improvement Act.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns a government proceeding to acquire land.
predicates.prior_division_bench_view_challenged: A party relied on an earlier division-bench decision that was itself under challenge before a higher court.
predicates.later_full_bench_disapproved_that_view: A later full bench of the same court disagreed with the earlier decision's reasoning.

issues.definition: In a land-acquisition proceeding, a challenged division-bench view disapproved by a later full bench does not control the outcome.
